item.text:
**Verdict:** Weaker.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Russia: Nations in Transit 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024) | Says Russia’s 2023 democracy score fell further: local autonomy eroded, electronic voting facilitated fraud, and the September 2023 regional/local elections lacked genuine opposition and were shaped by intimidation. The only weak counterpoint is that municipal councils still functioned as a thin opposition training ground, but under shrinking and tightly controlled space. | 4B.10; also 4B.1, 4B.2, 4B.4, 4B.9 |
| Russia: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024) | Describes 2023 as continued authoritarian consolidation: Putin’s system curtailed speech, used politicized arrests/prosecutions, and suppressed dissent after the Wagner mutiny and ICC warrant. This is strong evidence that political freedom and democratic resilience ended the year weaker, not stronger. | 4B.10; also 4B.6, 4B.8, 4B.9 |
| Russia: Nations in Transit 2023 Country Report | Freedom House | 2023 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2023) | Portrays Russia as a personalist dictatorship where independent media were effectively extinct, local autonomy had already been sharply curtailed, and opposition space was being drained. It gives only narrow residual counterevidence in some municipal councils, but overall the trajectory is plainly negative. | 4B.10; also 4B.4, 4B.6, 4B.8, 4B.9 |
| Russians vote in tightly controlled regional elections | Reuters | September 7, 2023 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russians-vote-in-tightlycontrolled-regional-elections-first-since-war-began-3169837) | Reports that the 2023 regional and local elections were tightly controlled, with opposition candidates blocked or withdrawing, election practices expanded in ways critics said helped falsify results, and strong employer pressure on turnout. This is procedural form without meaningful democratic resilience. | 4B.10; also 4B.1, 4B.2, 4B.8 |
| Russia arrests leader of vote monitoring group three weeks before regional polls | Reuters | August 18, 2023 | [link](https://uk.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-detains-leader-of-election-monitoring-group-3127724) | Says the arrest of Golos co-chair Grigory Melkonyants and raids on monitors’ homes appeared aimed at blocking scrutiny of the vote. That is direct evidence against electoral openness and against any strengthening of democratic oversight. | 4B.10; also 4B.2, 4B.4, 4B.9 |
| Russia designates The Moscow Times newspaper a “foreign agent” | Reuters | November 18, 2023 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-designates-the-moscow-times-newspaper-a-foreign-agent-3238256) | Shows the Justice Ministry imposing disclaimer, reporting, and self-disclosure burdens on an already blocked independent outlet. This is administrative pressure on journalism, not resilience-building. | 4B.10; also 4B.6, 4B.9 |
| Putin signs Russian law establishing electronic draft call-up | Reuters | April 14, 2023 | [link](https://www.yahoo.com/news/putin-signs-russian-law-establishing-195445933.html) | Putin’s electronic conscription law digitized draft notices and closed evasion loopholes, expanding state leverage over citizens. It is a digital control tool, not evidence of greater political freedom. | 4B.10; also 4B.9 |
| Anti-war challenger Duntsova barred from running against Russia’s Putin | Reuters | December 23, 2023 | [link](https://theprint.in/world/anti-war-challenger-duntsova-barred-from-running-against-russias-putin/1898291/) | The election commission rejected a credible anti-war challenger after she campaigned against the war and for political prisoners, clearing the field rather than opening it. That points against succession openness and democratic resilience. | 4B.10; also 4B.8, 4B.2 |

**Search gap:** I found no reliable evidence that Putin left Russia’s political freedom or democratic resilience stronger than he inherited it in 2023. The only partial counterevidence was formal or procedural: elections still occurred, and some municipal councils retained a narrow opposition-training role. Every source describing those formal channels also described heavy control, fraud, intimidation, censorship, surveillance, or administrative harassment.
